feedback.details: SprintCriterion in shared/types.ts (line 55) includes `type?: "behavioral" | "implementation"` as an optional field. SprintContract interface is unchanged. RegressionCriterion interface is also properly defined. Backward compatible — contracts without the field work fine since the type is optional.

CONTRACT_NEGOTIATION_GENERATOR_PROMPT (shared/prompts.ts line 386) includes the type field in the JSON example and explicit instructions to classify as 'behavioral' or 'implementation'. CONTRACT_NEGOTIATION_EVALUATOR_PROMPT (line 414) instructs validation of the type field. Static prompt constants (PLANNER_SYSTEM_PROMPT, GENERATOR_SYSTEM_PROMPT, EVALUATOR_SYSTEM_PROMPT) remain unchanged.

shared/regression.ts `accumulateRegressionCriteria` correctly filters `c.type === 'behavioral'` (line 37), excluding both 'implementation' and no-type criteria. Deduplication by name via Map (lines 43-56) with newer sprint replacing older. Called in harness.ts (line 664) after a sprint passes, gated by `!config.noBdd` (line 662).

regression.json is written as a JSON array of objects with name, description, threshold, and sprintNumber. Created on first accumulation, appended on subsequent sprints. The cleanHarnessArtifacts function (shared/files.ts lines 68-76) only cleans contracts/, feedback/, spec.md, and progress.json — regression.json is untouched. Test at regression.test.ts line 196 verifies this.

In harness.ts lines 537-546, when sprint > 1 and !config.noBdd, regression criteria are read and built into a '## Regression Criteria' section. This is injected as supplementaryContext into the evaluator prompt (evaluator.ts line 41). The section is clearly separated with its own header. When regression.json doesn't exist or is empty, readRegressionCriteria returns [] and buildRegressionSection returns '', so no section is added.

In harness.ts, both accumulation (line 662: `if (!config.noBdd)`) and injection (line 537: `if (!config.noBdd && sprint > 1)`) are gated on noBdd. When noBdd is true, regression.json is neither read nor written. Existing regression.json is not deleted. Implementation is correct.

shared/static-analysis.ts `detectStaticAnalysisCommands` reads package.json, checks for 'lint', 'typecheck', 'type-check' keys (line 4). Returns empty array on missing package.json, missing scripts field, or no matching keys — all via try/catch (line 29). No errors thrown. Detection reads from projectDir parameter, which in harness.ts is correctly set to config.workDir or app/ for greenfield.

In harness.ts lines 549-571, static analysis runs between generator completion and evaluator invocation. Commands are executed via Bun.spawnSync in the project directory. Output is injected under '## Static Analysis Results' section header. Non-zero exit codes don't prevent evaluator from running in soft mode. The subprocess is wrapped in try/catch (line 901). Uses Bun.spawnSync rather than async subprocess, which is a minor style inconsistency but functional.

When no commands are detected, runStaticAnalysis returns { output: '', failed: false } (line 877). The harness checks `if (staticAnalysisResult.output)` (line 551), so no section is added to the evaluator prompt. No error or warning is logged.

shared/static-analysis.ts `truncateStaticAnalysisOutput` (line 38) truncates to 4000 chars and appends '[output truncated — showing first 4000 chars of N total]'. Output at exactly 4000 chars is not truncated. Tests verify exact behavior including the total count.

The --lint-gate flag is parsed in config.ts (line 95) and stored as `lintGate?: boolean` on HarnessConfig (line 42). In harness.ts lines 552-568, when lintGate is set and any command failed, the evaluator is skipped, the attempt fails, and static analysis output is included in the feedback (overallSummary) passed to the next generator retry. When not set, output is still injected into evaluator (soft gate).

tests/regression.test.ts covers: (1) writing behavioral criteria (line 25), (2) excluding implementation (line 43) and no-type criteria (line 58), (3) reading and building section for evaluator (line 148-166), (4) deduplication by name (line 73), (5) --no-bdd skipping (line 168, simulated via local boolean), (6) regression.json surviving cleanHarnessArtifacts (line 196). All tests pass. The --no-bdd test simulates the flag rather than testing actual config integration, but functionally covers the requirement.

tests/static-analysis.test.ts covers: (1) command detection for lint, typecheck, type-check keys (lines 20-94), (2) graceful empty array for no package.json or no matching scripts (lines 69-94), (3) truncation at 4000 chars with warning message (lines 97-122), (4) lint-gate boolean logic (lines 124-147). The lint-gate tests verify the conditional logic pattern rather than actual harness integration, but they do test the expected behavior. All tests pass.

All 311 tests pass with `bun test` (0 failures). However, `tsc --noEmit` reveals 14+ TypeScript errors in tests/config.test.ts where the `lintGate` property is missing from ParsedCli objects passed to resolveConfig(). The ParsedCli interface now requires `lintGate: boolean`, but existing test callsites were not updated. While Bun's test runner is lenient and the tests pass at runtime, strict TypeScript compilation fails. This means existing tests are technically broken from a type-safety perspective.

New shared/ modules (regression.ts, static-analysis.ts) are clean: no 'any' assertions, async/await used in regression.ts, node:fs/promises for file ops, try/catch around file operations, named exports only. However, the ParsedCli interface change (adding required `lintGate` field) breaks TypeScript strict mode compatibility in existing tests/config.test.ts — 14+ compilation errors. The harness.ts uses Bun.spawnSync (sync subprocess) but wraps it in try/catch. The overall introduction of the `lintGate` field as required (not optional) on the internal ParsedCli is the root cause of the TS breakage.

overallSummary: The implementation of both BDD Regression Accumulation and Static Analysis Soft Gate features is functionally correct and well-structured. The core shared modules (regression.ts, static-analysis.ts) are clean, well-tested, and properly integrated into the harness. The contract negotiation prompts are correctly updated. However, the sprint fails due to TypeScript compilation errors: adding `lintGate` as a required field on ParsedCli broke 14+ existing test callsites in config.test.ts. While `bun test` passes (311/311), `tsc --noEmit` fails, violating both 'existing_tests_still_pass' (type errors in pre-existing test files) and 'type_safety_and_code_quality' (TypeScript strict mode incompatibility) criteria.
